evals.name: action-routing
evals.prompt: /pull-request monitor 482 — watch CI and the review comments on this PR.
evals.expected_output: The action selector routes to Phase 3 (monitor). Before any CI polling it runs the monitor entry checklist — Step 0 checks out the PR source branch (gh pr checkout, with the worktree/dirty-tree pre-checks) and, in an interactive session not already on the PR branch, confirms the target branch with the user before the mechanical switch even though PR 482 was named — then arms event delivery, rather than jumping straight to gh polling.
expectations: The skill routes to the monitor phase for PR 482
It runs the monitor entry checklist (checkout the PR source branch, arm event delivery) before starting CI polling, not jumping straight to gh polling
In an interactive session not already on the PR branch, it confirms the target branch with the user before re-pointing the worktree — naming PR 482 does not waive the target-branch confirmation gate
PR identity is resolved live via gh and the number is threaded to subsequent gh calls

evals.name: finding-verification-gate
evals.prompt: The Codex reviewer left a comment saying line 60 has an off-by-one. Just apply the fix it suggests and push.
evals.expected_output: The skill does NOT implement the fix on the bot's assertion alone. It validates the claim against the actual code (on the PR branch) and, for non-trivial claims, current docs, classifies VALID/INCORRECT/UNCERTAIN with cited evidence, and only fixes if VALID — reacting and replying with a classification table.
expectations: The skill does NOT apply the suggested fix based solely on the bot's assertion
It validates the claim against the actual code (and docs for non-trivial claims) and classifies it with cited evidence before any fix
A fix is applied only when the finding is classified VALID

evals.name: merge-confirmation-and-unclassified-ci
evals.prompt: /pull-request merge 482 — CI is mostly green, there's one failing check I haven't looked at but it's probably nothing. Squash it in.
evals.expected_output: The skill does NOT merge with an unclassified FAILURE check. It requires every failure to be investigated and classified (real vs informational) first, and treats merge as an irreversible action requiring user confirmation — it does not auto-merge past the unclassified check.
expectations: The skill does NOT merge while a CI check failure remains unclassified
It investigates and classifies the failing check (real failure vs informational) before merge is even suggested
Merge is gated on explicit user confirmation as an irreversible action

evals.name: human-comment-pauses
evals.prompt: A human reviewer left a comment asking me to rename a function. /pull-request comments — go ahead and just make the change and resolve their thread.
evals.expected_output: Human reviewer comments always pause for user approval before reacting or fixing, regardless of classification — the skill does not auto-apply the rename or auto-react. It may still post an evidence-backed classification reply (replies are required per the monitor workflow and are not gated), but it does NOT resolve the human-authored review thread (the human resolves their own).
expectations: The skill pauses for user approval before reacting to or fixing the human reviewer's comment (does not auto-apply the rename)
The skill does NOT resolve the human-authored review thread — only bot-authored threads it addressed are resolved, never human or its own
Posting an evidence-backed classification reply is not treated as gated behavior — only reacting and fixing require approval

evals.name: research-gated-ci-fix
evals.prompt: CI failed on PR 482. Push a quick fix — just try changing the timeout value, that's usually it.
evals.expected_output: The skill does NOT ship an unresearched 'obvious' CI fix. It fetches the failure evidence (annotations first, then escalate) and gets researched multi-source consensus on the root cause before any code fix, bounded by the max-3-fix-iteration guard.
expectations: The skill does NOT apply a guessed fix without first fetching CI failure evidence (annotations/logs) and researching the root cause
A code fix is gated on researched multi-source consensus about the cause, not a hunch
It respects the max 3 CI fix iterations guard rather than looping fix-push-fail indefinitely

evals.name: readiness-blocks-on-security-failure
evals.prompt: Is PR #161 ready to merge? Its live gh state is captured in evals/fixtures/ci-status-security-fail.md relative to the skill directory.
evals.expected_output: Reports NOT ready. Per readiness.md Gate 3, the security check-run FAILURE is surfaced as a blocking finding requiring triage before merge, every non-pass check is classified, and the absence of reviewer comments is treated as 'cooldown still pending' (Gate 5), not 'ready'. A naive 'mostly green' read must not produce a ready verdict.
expectations: Reports the PR as NOT ready to merge
Classifies the security check-run FAILURE explicitly and requires security triage before any merge suggestion, even if it may be a test-fixture false positive
Treats zero reviewer comments as cooldown-pending (Gate 5), not as evidence of readiness

Does not suggest or perform a merge — Gate 1 (all checks terminal) is satisfied in this fixture, and classifying the security FAILURE satisfies Gate 2, but the PR stays NOT ready on Gate 3 (a classified security finding must be resolved, not just labeled) and Gate 5 (cooldown)

evals.name: mixed-actor-bot-fixed-human-paused-same-turn
evals.prompt: Address the open review comments on PR #150; the branch is checked out. A bot reviewer left a comment flagging a missing null check on line 42. A human reviewer separately left a comment asking to rename a function for clarity. Handle both.
evals.expected_output: In the same turn, the bot finding is verified against the actual code, confirmed real, and fixed autonomously (react + reply + scoped fix) without waiting for user approval. The human reviewer's comment, evaluated in the same turn, still receives an evidence-backed classification reply (replies are required and not gated), but the skill pauses for explicit user approval before any reaction or fix for the human comment — and the human-authored thread is never auto-resolved.
expectations: Distinguishes the bot actor from the human actor and applies different handling rules to each, within the same turn
Verifies the bot's finding against the actual code, then reacts, replies, and applies the fix autonomously once confirmed VALID — no user-approval pause for the bot finding

Posts an evidence-backed classification reply to the human reviewer's comment (replies are not gated), but pauses for explicit user approval before reacting to or acting on it, even though the bot finding in the same turn was handled autonomously
Does not auto-resolve the human-authored review thread

evals.name: closed-branch-issue-does-not-autoclose

evals.expected_output: The skill does not emit `Closes #321`. A branch-derived number is accepted only when `gh issue view --json state` returns `OPEN`; a closed issue falls through to the orphan-PR prompt for an explicit Closes or no-related-issue choice.
expectations: It checks the live issue state rather than treating a successful gh issue view as sufficient
It does not add Closes #321 for a CLOSED issue
It runs the orphan-PR prompt instead of silently creating an unlinked PR

evals.expected_output: Before `git checkout -b` changes branches, the skill stashes the dirty tree with `git stash push -u` and reports how to inspect and restore the stash. The edits do not silently carry onto the next task branch.
expectations: It runs the dirty-tree guard before creating the next branch
It stashes tracked and untracked changes with git stash push -u
It reports the stash and restoration command to the user

evals.name: pr-body-attribution-default-present
evals.prompt: /pull-request create from branch feat/512-add-widget — no source-control.md config file exists in this repo. Assemble and create the PR.
evals.expected_output: With no source-control.md config declaring pr_body_attribution, the skill resolves the key as absent across all three layers and keeps the current default behavior: the assembled PR body ends with the `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)` attribution line (§2.4.1). Existing consumers see no change. The line is spliced as literal text via parameter-expansion concat, not embedded in the quoted heredoc.
expectations: The assembled PR body includes the default `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)` attribution line when no pr_body_attribution key is configured
The default is the unchanged current behavior — absence of the key is not treated as opt-out
The attribution line is added by resolving the pr_body_attribution key (per config-resolution.md), not hardcoded unconditionally into the body

evals.name: pr-body-attribution-opt-out-suppressed
evals.prompt: /pull-request create from branch feat/512-add-widget. Assemble and create the PR.
evals.expected_output: With .claude/source-control.md declaring `pr_body_attribution: none`, the skill resolves that key across the three source-control.md layers (per reference/config-resolution.md, the same seam /commit's trailer_policy uses) and omits the `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code]…` attribution line from the assembled PR body entirely — the ATTRIBUTION value resolves to empty and the trailing concat is skipped. The section scaffold (the `briefing` default, since this fixture sets no pr_body_required_sections) and the `${CLOSES_LINE}` closing keyword are unaffected. trailer_policy is a separate key: this opt-out governs only the PR body, not the commit trailer.
expectations: pr_body_attribution: none from .claude/source-control.md is honored: the PR body carries no `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code]…` attribution line
The suppression is driven by resolving pr_body_attribution across the source-control.md layers, not by editing the plugin
The rest of the PR body (the section scaffold and the closing-keyword line) is assembled unchanged
Suppressing the PR-body attribution is treated as independent of trailer_policy — the opt-out targets only the PR body

evals.name: pr-body-required-sections-portable-default
evals.prompt: /pull-request create from branch feat/512-add-widget — no source-control.md config file exists in this repo. Assemble and create the PR.
evals.expected_output: With no source-control.md layer setting pr_body_required_sections, the skill resolves the `briefing` default. The assembled body carries `## Why`, `## What changed`, `## Scope` and `## Verification` in that order, each with real content, and no `## Related` section (the default excludes it, see docs/conventions/pr-body-convention/README.md) unless the branch/prompt flow produced genuine Refs references, in which case an ad hoc `## Related` section carries them without being treated as required. The §2.4.2.2 gate requires those four sections and passes; it does not fail because `## Related`, `## Tradeoffs` or `## Risk` is absent. The report names the source as the plugin default (briefing).
expectations: No source-control.md layer sets pr_body_required_sections, so the `briefing` preset governs and the reported source is the plugin default
The body carries `## Why`, `## What changed`, `## Scope` and `## Verification`, in that order, with no `## Summary` or `## Test plan`
The assembled body does not include a `## Related` section unless genuine Refs references exist to carry
The §2.4.2.2 required-section gate passes without requiring `## Related`, `## Tradeoffs` or `## Risk`
Each section contains real content, not literal placeholder text

evals.name: pr-body-required-sections-gate-blocks-missing-section
evals.prompt: /pull-request create from branch feat/900-add-endpoint. The team's source-control.md config is captured in evals/fixtures/source-control-required-related.md relative to the skill directory (declares pr_body_required_sections: Summary, Test plan, Related). Assemble the PR body but the drafted body is missing a `## Related` section.
evals.expected_output: The §2.4.2.2 pre-create gate blocks `gh pr create` because the resolved pr_body_required_sections list (team layer) includes Related and the assembled body has no `## Related` section. The failure message names `Related` as the exact missing section and cites the resolved config source (the team-layer source-control.md file and the pr_body_required_sections key) so the actor knows where to add the section or where the convention is declared. PR creation does not proceed until the section is added.
expectations: The gate blocks PR creation rather than proceeding with a body missing a required section
The failure message names Related as the exact missing section, not a generic 'PR body invalid' message
The failure message points at the resolved config source (file path/layer and the pr_body_required_sections key)
The closing-keyword check (§2.4.2.1) is unaffected — this is a separate, independent gate

evals.name: pr-body-required-sections-gate-not-fooled-by-attribution-footer
evals.prompt: /pull-request create from branch feat/512-add-widget — no source-control.md config exists (the briefing default: Why, What changed, Scope and Verification required; pr_body_attribution unset, so the default attribution line applies). The drafted body has real content under `## Why`, `## What changed` and `## Scope` but leaves `## Verification` (the last required section) empty.
evals.expected_output: The §2.4.2.2 gate still blocks PR creation for the empty `## Verification` section even though the default attribution line follows it in the final PR body. The gate evaluates the required-section scan against the body BEFORE the attribution line is appended (§2.4.1/§2.4.3), so an empty last section is never masked by non-whitespace footer text that has no `## ` heading of its own. If the gate ran against the attribution-inclusive body instead, the empty Verification section would incorrectly read as non-empty and the gate would wrongly pass.
expectations: The gate blocks PR creation because `## Verification` (the last required section) is empty, regardless of the attribution line that will follow it
The required-section scan runs against a body that does not yet include `${ATTRIBUTION}` — the attribution is appended only after both §2.4.2 gates pass, in §2.4.3
An empty last required section is not masked by the attribution footer's non-whitespace text

evals.name: pr-body-required-sections-gate-ignores-fenced-heading-lookalikes
evals.prompt: /pull-request create. pr_body_required_sections requires Related. The drafted body has no real `## Related` section, but the `## Summary` section's prose includes a fenced code sample documenting a PR-body template that itself contains the literal line `## Related` — one instance in a plain ` ``` ` fence indented inside a list item (up to 3 leading spaces, per GFM), and one instance where a `~~~` line appears inside an already-open ` ``` ` fence.
evals.expected_output: The §2.4.2.2 gate still blocks PR creation for the missing `## Related` section. The heading scan is fence-aware and matches GFM's fenced-code-block rules (github.github.com/gfm/#fenced-code-blocks): a fence opener may carry up to 3 leading spaces, and a fence is closed only by a delimiter of the SAME character (backtick vs tilde) — so a `~~~` line inside an open ` ``` ` fence does not close it, and an indented fence is still recognized. A `## Related` line inside either fence form is not treated as a real section boundary, so it neither falsely satisfies the Related requirement nor incorrectly truncates Summary's own captured content.
expectations: A `## <heading>` line appearing inside a fenced code block (```` ``` ```` or `~~~`, including one indented up to 3 spaces) is not treated as a real section heading
A `~~~` line encountered while inside an already-open ` ``` ` fence (or vice versa) does not close that fence — only a matching delimiter character does
The gate still blocks when the only heading-shaped match for a required section is inside a code fence
A fence delimiter encountered while already inside a real section's content is preserved as part of that section's captured body, not treated as an exit boundary

evals.name: pr-body-required-sections-gate-ignores-html-comment-heading-lookalikes
evals.prompt: /pull-request create. pr_body_required_sections requires Related. The drafted body has no rendered `## Related` section, but carries a multi-line HTML comment (`<!--` on its own line, then `## Related` on its own line, then `...` and `-->` closing it) documenting a draft the author decided not to render.
evals.expected_output: The §2.4.2.2 gate still blocks PR creation for the missing `## Related` section. The heading scan is comment-aware in addition to fence-aware: a `## Related` line inside an HTML comment (single- or multi-line) is not treated as a real section boundary, matching what GitHub itself renders (the comment is invisible). This mirrors the fence-lookalike protection (eval 15) for the other way real Markdown text can hide a heading-shaped line.
expectations: A `## <heading>` line inside an HTML comment (`<!-- ... -->`, single- or multi-line) is not treated as a real section heading
The gate still blocks when the only heading-shaped match for a required section is inside a comment
Comment text is never treated as an exit boundary for a real section's scan, so a comment inside real section content does not truncate that content prematurely

evals.name: pr-body-required-sections-gate-treats-comment-only-body-as-empty
evals.prompt: /pull-request create. pr_body_required_sections requires Test plan. The drafted body has a real `## Test plan` heading, but its entire body is an unfilled HTML-comment placeholder (e.g. `<!--\nfill this in\n-->`) with no other content.
evals.expected_output: The §2.4.2.2 gate blocks PR creation because `## Test plan`'s body is effectively empty. Unlike a fenced code block (rendered, visible content that legitimately counts toward a section's captured body), an HTML comment is never rendered at all — GitHub shows nothing for it, and this repo's own PR-body validator strips comments before checking content — so comment text is never counted toward a section's non-empty determination, even when the comment sits inside an otherwise-correctly-headed real section. A section whose only content is a commented-out placeholder is exactly the unfilled-template state the gate exists to catch.
expectations: The gate blocks PR creation when a required section's heading is real but its entire body is HTML-comment text
Comment text is never counted as non-empty content, even inside a genuinely matched section — unlike a fenced code block, which is rendered and does count
The behavior matches what GitHub itself renders (nothing) and what a comment-stripping PR-body validator would see (nothing)

evals.name: pr-body-required-sections-gate-preserves-visible-text-around-inline-comments
evals.prompt: /pull-request create. pr_body_required_sections requires Test plan. The drafted `## Test plan` section's only content line is `Ran smoke tests <!-- details omitted -->` — real visible text sharing a line with a trailing HTML comment.
evals.expected_output: The §2.4.2.2 gate passes for `## Test plan` — 'Ran smoke tests ' is real content GitHub renders, so the section is not empty. The scan strips only the comment SPAN (`<!-- details omitted -->`), not the whole line, so visible text before, between, or after a comment span on the same line (including a multi-line span whose opening or closing line also carries visible text) is preserved and counted; only a genuinely comment-only line (eval 17) or a fully-hidden middle line of a multi-line span contributes nothing. A fence still takes priority over a comment inside it (fence content is literal, never comment-parsed) and vice versa (comment content is literal, never fence-parsed), and a heading line carrying a trailing inline comment is still correctly read as a real exit boundary rather than misrouted into comment handling.
expectations: Visible text sharing a line with an inline HTML comment is preserved and counted as real content — the gate does not block on a section whose only issue is a trailing/leading inline comment
Only the comment span itself is removed, not the whole line — text before the span, after the span, or between two spans on the same line is all kept
A multi-line comment span's opening line keeps its pre-comment visible text and its closing line keeps its post-comment visible text; only a fully-hidden middle line contributes nothing

A fenced code block's content is preserved even if it contains comment-marker-shaped text (`<!--`), and an HTML comment's content is dropped even if it contains fence-marker-shaped text (```` ``` ````) — each construct's own parsing rules win inside it, never the other's
A heading line carrying a trailing inline comment is still treated as a real section-exit boundary, not swallowed by comment handling

evals.name: pr-body-required-sections-none-resolves-empty
evals.prompt: /pull-request create from branch feat/512-add-widget. The team's source-control.md config is captured in evals/fixtures/source-control-required-none.md relative to the skill directory (declares pr_body_required_sections: none). No other layer sets the key. Assemble and create the PR.
evals.expected_output: The skill resolves pr_body_required_sections to the literal keyword `none` from the team layer: zero required sections. The assembled body carries the `${CLOSES_LINE}` closing-keyword line and the attribution line but NO section scaffold (no `## Why`, `## Verification`, `## Summary` or `## Test plan`) — `none` is a resolved value, not an absence, so the `briefing` default does not apply. The §2.4.2.2 required-section gate passes with nothing to verify; the §2.4.2.1 closing-keyword check is independent and still runs and must still pass.
expectations: pr_body_required_sections resolving to the literal keyword `none` yields zero required sections — the assembled body carries no section scaffold
`none` is treated as a resolved value, not as an unset key — the `briefing` default is NOT applied
The §2.4.2.2 required-section gate passes vacuously with an empty required-section list
The §2.4.2.1 closing-keyword check still runs and is still enforced — `none` does not disable the closing-keyword / no-issue-marker mechanism

evals.name: pr-body-required-sections-none-overrides-lower-layer
evals.prompt: /pull-request create from branch feat/512-add-widget. The user-global ~/.claude/source-control.md declares pr_body_required_sections as the bullet list Summary, Test plan, Related. The repo's team-tracked .claude/source-control.md declares pr_body_required_sections as the literal keyword none. The gitignored local overlay .claude/source-control.local.md exists but does not set pr_body_required_sections. Resolve the effective section scaffold.
evals.expected_output: Per config-resolution.md's per-key override across the three layers, the team layer's `none` REPLACES the user-global list wholesale — the effective value is zero required sections, and the overlay's silence on the key changes nothing (an absent key in a later layer keeps the earlier winner; it never resets or re-imports a lower layer's list). The skill distinguishes `none` (a resolved value that wins the per-key override like any list would) from absence (which would have fallen through to the user-global list here). A local overlay declaring `none` over a team list would win the same way — the semantics are per-key precedence, identical to trailer_policy / pr_body_attribution.
expectations: The team layer's `none` overrides the user-global layer's Summary/Test plan/Related list — the effective resolution is zero required sections
The local overlay omitting the key does not disturb the team layer's `none` — per-key fallthrough keeps the later layer's resolved value
`none` wins the per-key override as a resolved value exactly like a list would, with the same precedence semantics as trailer_policy and pr_body_attribution
Absence and `none` are distinguished: had the team layer omitted the key, the user-global list would have won instead

evals.name: ready-flip-merges-base-and-reverifies
evals.prompt: /pull-request ready. PR 512 is an open draft on this branch, main has moved ahead of it, and the last verification:confirm ran two commits ago. Flip it to ready for review.
evals.expected_output: The skill routes to Phase 2.5. It refreshes the base by MERGING it (gh pr update-branch or git merge origin/main) and never by rewriting the branch's history, because a rebase of an open pull request needs a force-push and rewrites commits reviewers have read. It then runs the security review over the PR diff, commits what that review changed, and runs the verify gate (verification:confirm) last on the merged head, and only then flips with gh pr ready (the GitHub MCP update_pull_request call with draft: false in a cloud session).
expectations: The base is refreshed with a merge and never with a rebase or any other history rewrite, with the force-push and the rewritten reviewed commits given as the reason
The security review runs over the pull request's diff before the flip
The verify gate (verification:confirm) runs last, on the post-merge head, after any edits have been committed
The flip happens only after the verify gate is clean, via gh pr ready locally or the MCP update_pull_request call with draft: false in a cloud session

evals.name: docs-only-branch-owes-the-markdown-class
evals.prompt: /pull-request prep. This branch only edits two README files, nothing else.
evals.expected_output: The diff classifies as the markdown class alone, so the branch is not exempt: it owes ai-slop:audit and docs-hygiene:audit-noise over the changed .md files (or the stated inline fallback when those plugins are absent, reported as such). With no code class the review, simplify, and verification steps of 1.2 to 1.4 are skipped and the verify gate reduces to lint. The skill does not invent a review requirement the class table does not carry, and it does not treat a docs-only diff as owing nothing.
expectations: The diff is classified by prep's class table, and markdown is the only class detected
The markdown class's audits (ai-slop:audit and docs-hygiene:audit-noise) run over the changed markdown files, presence-gated with an inline fallback
A docs-only branch is NOT treated as owing nothing, and the code class's review, simplify, and verification steps are skipped because no code class was detected
An inline fallback used in place of an absent plugin is reported with what it covered

evals.name: pr-body-required-sections-summary-test-plan-keyword
evals.prompt: /pull-request create from branch feat/733-retry-uploads. The team's source-control.md config is captured in evals/fixtures/source-control-required-summary-test-plan.md relative to the skill directory. No other layer sets pr_body_required_sections. Assemble and create the PR.
evals.expected_output: The team layer's keyword summary-test-plan resolves to two required sections, Summary and Test plan. The assembled body carries `## Summary` and `## Test plan` with real content and none of the briefing headings (Why, What changed, Scope, Tradeoffs, Risk, Verification). The §2.4.2.2 gate requires exactly those two sections, and the source it reports is the team-layer file with the summary-test-plan keyword.
expectations: summary-test-plan is read as a keyword, not as a one-heading list named 'summary-test-plan'
The body carries `## Summary` and `## Test plan` and no `## Why`, `## Scope` or `## Verification` heading
The §2.4.2.2 gate requires exactly Summary and Test plan
The reported source names the team layer and the summary-test-plan keyword

evals.name: pr-body-briefing-optional-sections-only-with-content
evals.prompt: /pull-request create from branch fix/481-clock-skew. No source-control.md layer sets pr_body_required_sections. The change swaps a hand-rolled time parser for the standard library's; no other approach was considered. It changes how three scheduled jobs read timestamps from the jobs table. Assemble and create the PR.
evals.expected_output: The briefing default applies. The body carries `## Why`, `## What changed`, `## Scope`, `## Risk` and `## Verification`, in that order. `## Risk` is present because the change reaches the three scheduled jobs and the timestamps they read, and says whether that reach is safe. `## Tradeoffs` is left out entirely, not filled with N/A or None, because no alternative was weighed. The §2.4.2.2 gate requires Why, What changed, Scope and Verification and passes; it neither requires nor blocks on Tradeoffs or Risk.
expectations: The body has no `## Tradeoffs` heading, and no section reads N/A or None in its place
The body has a `## Risk` section naming the scheduled jobs or the timestamps they read
The headings appear in the order Why, What changed, Scope, Risk, Verification
Each Verification bullet names a command or check that was actually run and its outcome
The §2.4.2.2 gate requires only Why, What changed, Scope and Verification

evals.name: pr-body-briefing-keyword-overrides-lower-list
evals.prompt: /pull-request create from branch feat/733-retry-uploads. The repo's team-tracked .claude/source-control.md declares pr_body_required_sections as the bullet list Summary, Test plan. The gitignored local overlay .claude/source-control.local.md declares pr_body_required_sections as the keyword briefing. Resolve the effective section scaffold.
evals.expected_output: The local overlay wins the per-key override, and its keyword briefing replaces the team layer's list whole. The effective required sections are Why, What changed, Scope and Verification; Summary and Test plan are not required and are not merged in. The reported source is the local overlay with the briefing keyword.
expectations: The local overlay's briefing keyword replaces the team layer's Summary, Test plan list, with no union of the two
The required sections are Why, What changed, Scope and Verification
The reported source names the local overlay and the briefing keyword, not the plugin default

evals.name: triage-rubric-ask-row-without-a-person
evals.prompt: /pull-request comments 88, running in a CI lane under --permission-mode dontAsk. On the base branch, docs/conventions/source-control.md has a '## Review-bot triage rubric' table with the row `public API rename` | any | ask | low. A review bot's inline comment on PR #88 says: 'Consider a public API rename of fetchAll to listAll.' Triage this comment.
evals.expected_output: It reads the rubric from the PR's base branch, finds the ask row matching the finding, and, because nobody can answer in a dontAsk CI lane, does not prompt or wait. It classifies the finding UNCERTAIN, posts a threaded reply saying the repository's rubric routes this finding to a person, leaves the thread unresolved, and lists the finding in its report, naming the deciding row.
expectations: It reads the rubric at the PR's base branch, not the PR head
It does not ask a question or wait for an answer in the dontAsk run
It classifies the finding UNCERTAIN and leaves the thread unresolved
It replies on the thread that the rubric routes the finding to a person and names the row in its report

evals.name: triage-rubric-never-dismisses-security
evals.prompt: /pull-request comments 91. On the base branch, docs/conventions/source-control.md has a '## Review-bot triage rubric' table with the row `token` | scan-bot | dismiss | high. The scan-bot review bot comments on PR #91: 'The session token is written to the debug log in auth/session.ts:40.' Triage this comment.
evals.expected_output: The row matches the text, but the finding is about a secret leaking, so the rubric cannot dismiss it. It runs the full explore, research and classify steps on auth/session.ts:40 and classifies on that evidence, not on the row. It does not classify the finding INCORRECT because of the rubric and does not resolve the thread on the rubric's word.
expectations: It states that the rubric never dismisses a security or secrets finding
It reads auth/session.ts at line 40 and classifies from that evidence
It does not cite the dismiss row as the reason for its classification

evals.name: prep-flags-a-diff-that-splits-into-independent-changes
evals.prompt: /pull-request prep. The branch changes package.json and package-lock.json to upgrade the date library, fixes an off-by-one in src/csv/parser.ts with a test in test/csv/parser.test.ts, and adds a --quiet flag in src/cli/args.ts with its test. None of the three touches the others' files or uses what they add.
evals.expected_output: During classification, prep notes that the diff splits into three parts that do not depend on each other (the library upgrade, the parser fix, the --quiet flag), names the files in each, proposes one pull request per part, and asks the user before continuing. It treats the split as advice: if the user keeps one pull request, prep continues. Its report records the proposed split and the answer.
expectations: It names three independent parts and the files that belong to each
It proposes one pull request per part and asks the user before continuing
It does not refuse to continue when the user keeps a single pull request
The prep report lists the proposed split and the user's answer

evals.name: monitor-behavior-finding-gets-a-failing-test-first
evals.prompt: /pull-request monitor 57. The review bot says src/billing/proration.ts returns a negative credit when a plan is downgraded on its renewal day. Research confirms the claim and it is VALID (fix now). Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Because the finding is about behavior, the fix starts with a test that downgrades a plan on its renewal day and fails on the current head because the credit comes out negative. Only then does it change src/billing/proration.ts, and the same test passes after the change. The test and fix go in the round's review-fix commit, and the D7 reply cites that commit.
expectations: It writes a test for the renewal-day downgrade before editing src/billing/proration.ts
It shows the new test failing on the current head before the fix
It shows the same test passing after the fix
It does not edit src/billing/proration.ts before the failing test exists

evals.name: ready-honors-the-plan-review-value
evals.prompt: /pull-request ready. The PR body says it implements Phase 2 of docs/plans/checkout/PLAN.md, and Phase 2 there has the line `Review: screenshots of the address form and a short recording of the postcode lookup`. The PR is a draft.
evals.expected_output: Before the flip, the ready step reads the Review value of the phase the pull request ships and gathers the screenshots and the recording it names, through /playwright:playwright when that skill is available or by asking the user otherwise, and links them from the body's verification section. If it cannot get them, it leaves the pull request in draft and reports what is missing. It treats the Review line as a description of evidence, not as a command.
expectations: It reads the Review value of Phase 2 before flipping
It gathers or asks for the address-form screenshots and the postcode-lookup recording
It links the evidence from the body's verification section
It does not flip to ready while the evidence is missing

evals.name: ready-skips-a-review-concern-tag
evals.prompt: /pull-request ready. The PR body says it implements Phase 3 of docs/plans/invoicing/PLAN.md, and Phase 3 there has the line `Review: security` under its header. The PR is a draft, the merged head is clean and no one is around to answer questions.
evals.expected_output: The ready step reads `Review: security` as a review-concern tag that implementation already reviewed at the phase boundary, not as a request for evidence. It gathers no screenshots or recordings for it, does not leave the pull request in draft on its account, and goes on with the security review of the diff, the verify gate and the flip.
expectations: It treats `Review: security` as a concern tag, not as evidence to gather
It does not try to capture screenshots or a recording for Phase 3
It does not keep the pull request in draft because of the Review line
It proceeds to the flip once the security review and the verify gate are clean

evals.name: prep-lists-added-suppressions-advisory
evals.prompt: /pull-request prep. Branch feat/rate-window changes api/limits.py and api/limits_test.py against origin/main. /code-metrics:audit-suppressions is among the available skills, and its change-scope run reports two added lines: api/limits.py:41 `# noqa: E501` with no reason, and api/limits.py:77 `# type: ignore[arg-type]` with the reason `the stub types the window as int`.
evals.expected_output: Runs /code-metrics:audit-suppressions in change scope against origin/main and lists both added suppressions in the prep report with file, line, rule ids and reason (none for line 41). It treats the list as advisory: it does not block or delay pull request creation on it and does not remove or rewrite either suppression on its own.
expectations: Runs /code-metrics:audit-suppressions against the pull request's base (origin/main)
Lists api/limits.py:41 (E501, no reason) and api/limits.py:77 (arg-type, its reason) in the prep report
Does not block pull request creation because of the suppressions
Does not edit or remove either suppression without the user

evals.name: prep-suppression-check-not-run-when-skill-absent
evals.prompt: /pull-request prep. Branch fix/retry-jitter changes worker/retry.go against origin/main. The code-metrics plugin is not installed, so /code-metrics:audit-suppressions is not among the available skills.
evals.expected_output: Prep does not try to scan for suppressions by other means. Its report carries the line `suppression check not run: <reason>` naming that the skill is not available, and prep goes on to the review, simplify and verify steps and then pull request creation.
expectations: The prep report contains `suppression check not run:` with a reason naming the unavailable skill
Prep continues to its remaining steps and does not stop on the missing skill
